[ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r13] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · بعضهم | reports | Some restrict the hardship to earning the means of livelihood, which they regard as men’s responsibility.

[ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r5] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Calling her Adam’s wife rather than naming Hawwa adds aversion to Satan and strengthens the warning.
[ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r6] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · بعضهم | reports | One explanation is that Satan’s enmity arose simply from envy; Satan and his followers were the first to envy.
[ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r7] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · بعضهم | reports | Another explanation contrasts the old, ignorant Satan with the young, learned Adam; the ignorant are characteristically enemies of the learned.
[ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r8] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · بعضهم | reports | A third explanation is the opposition of their origins: Satan was created from fire, Adam from clay, and Hawwa from Adam.
[ALUSI-FULL:v16p270#2/r9] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The prohibition means they must not let Satan become the cause of their expulsion; it indirectly forbids placing themselves where he can expel them.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r1] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Adam’s creation and the angels’ prostration were already related in al-Baqara and al-Aʿraf; Ibn ʿĀshūr focuses here on what is distinctive in this sura’s wording.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r2] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | إن هذا points contemptuously to Satan; the author compares it with the pagans’ dismissive question about the man criticizing their gods. | mentions 21:36

[IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r5] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Satan envies both because God gave them knowledge of names, the basis of thought leading to guidance and speech that enables instruction; this frustrates his seduction of them and their descendants. | mentions 2:31
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r6] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Satan believed himself more deserving of honor than Adam and became resentful when ordered to prostrate to him.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r7] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The warning follows from Satan’s hostility: an enemy does not want his opponent’s well-being, so Adam and Eve must beware of being expelled.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r8] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The prohibition is phrased as Satan’s act, a pointed indirect way of telling Adam not to be swayed by means of expulsion; it does not mean merely that he must prevent news of his act reaching God.
